title: Obsidian: The Thinking Person's Set Up (FULL SET UP)
author: Vicky Zhao
summary: Argues that most people retain nothing from what they consume because they never process it, so the knowledge is wasted the moment the book closes or the podcast ends. An Obsidian Zettelkasten fixes this specifically because it forces processing — capture, rephrase in your own words, connect, tag toward an output, then revise — turning input into output rather than hoarding. The system must stay deliberately simple: under 1% of your time spent tweaking it, no bulk import of old notes, and synced across every device or capture dies at the moment of the idea. Explicitly NOT an AI setup: this one exists to protect and grow human thinking.
takeaways: Three non-negotiables: spend under 1% of your time tweaking the system; never bulk-import your existing notes; sync across every device you use.
Start from the single note that is top-of-mind right now and build bottom-up — important ideas prove themselves by being referenced again, and the rest can be let go.
Sync options: paid Obsidian Sync (one click, official) or free via iCloud or Dropbox. She uses iCloud and is transitioning to Obsidian Sync.
Five-step process: capture → process → connect → create output → improve on feedback, demonstrated live on Alan Watts's The Book.
Atomic discipline shown concretely: one chapter held about six distinct 'fictional belief' ideas, so she writes six linked notes rather than one.

Two kinds of connection: to related ideas (linking Watts's opposites-are-not-conflicts to Fitzgerald's first-rate-intelligence line), and to a dedicated source note so everything from one book gathers via backlinks.
Tagging is output-oriented, not topical: she rejects tags like 'philosophy' and instead tags by intended output (question, quote, anecdote, study) and status (research, draft, published).
Obsidian titles cannot contain / \ or : — use a dash instead.
Three ways to search: Quick Switcher (Cmd+O, titles), Global Search (Cmd+Shift+F, full text), and semantic search via Smart Connections.
quotes: So, this is my Zettelkasten, my second brain... and the goal is simple, get off the consumption hamster wheel and take input, actually turn it into output.
The number one problem people have is they continuously tweak the system, try out new features, try out new plugins, but actually don't spend enough time working on the ideas.
This is not a personal wiki for AI... this is really not for AI to read, but for me to capture the ideas, process the ideas, create output from the input.
People are saying, 'Oh, Obsidian won the AI war,' because it uses MD files.
The test of first-rate intelligence is to be able to hold two opposite ideas and still be able to function.
bestIdeas: The 1% rule as a forcing function against system procrastination — cap infrastructure time to protect content time. Applies to any personal tool, LifeOS included.
Start from what is live now instead of bulk-importing — avoids the second-brain graveyard; importance is proven by re-reference, not declared upfront.
Output-oriented tagging reframes tags as a queue for future work rather than a filing scheme, which is what actually solves 'I have notes but don't know what to do with them'.
Dedicated source notes with backlinks give you an automatic bibliography and stop orphaned ideas losing their origin.
Semantic search as a memory prosthetic — weak links between old and new notes surface without perfect recall.
tools: Obsidian — the core app, plain markdown files in a folder.
Obsidian Sync — official paid cross-device sync; iCloud or Dropbox as the free alternative.
Smart Connections — community plugin giving AI-assisted semantic search over the vault (used 2+ years).
Templates (core plugin) — reusable note structures such as her Idea Compass.
Whisper Flow — dictation, so notes can be spoken rather than typed.
Quick Switcher (Cmd+O) and Global Search (Cmd+Shift+F) — built-in search.
method: Rules first: under 1% time tweaking, no bulk import, sync everywhere.
Setup: download Obsidian, create a vault (just a folder), create notes as markdown files.
Capture — new note, descriptive title, no / \ or : in the name.
Process — rephrase in your own words, one idea per note.
Connect — [[wikilink]] to related ideas, and to a dedicated source note.
Create output — tag by intended output type and by status.
Improve — revisit tagged notes, expand with quotes and ideas found later, import older writing as it becomes relevant.

Optional: enable Smart Connections; set a templates folder (Idea Compass: North=theme, South=where it leads, West=similar, East=opposing); set the attachment folder and turn on 'automatically update internal links'.
